chains.title: TCF7L2 binds alt C more at the 8q24 enhancer and increases MYC

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the alt C allele more strongly than the ref T allele. TCF7L2 is the best-supported Wnt effector at the 8q24.21 CRC enhancer; the variant is ~57 bp from rs6983267 in a known TCF7L2-bound enhancer, and the T>C change is predicted to alter a TCF/LEF site. No QBiC-SELEX model is supplied for this exact variant here, so this is a motif- and locus-biology-based selection, not a direct affinity measurement.
rs73706717 lies in a distal 8q24 enhancer that is active in colorectal cancer cells and can be occupied by TCF7L2; the C allele increases TCF7L2 occupancy at this element.
The 8q24 enhancer regulates MYC, the principal target gene in this locus; increased TCF7L2 occupancy at the C allele increases MYC transcription.
HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells have active Wnt/TCF7L2 signaling and open chromatin at the 8q24.21 enhancer, making this a relevant cell context.
Higher TCF7L2 binding at the alt C allele increases MYC expression and colorectal cancer risk, assuming TCF7L2 acts as an activator in this enhancer context.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP shows C > T occupancy at rs73706717.
The C allele increases enhancer reporter activity in HCT116 cells.
MYC expression is higher on the C allele or in C-bearing enhancer reporter cells.
The C allele is the risk-associated allele in this model.
falsified_if: TCF7L2 binds equally to T and C alleles in a direct binding assay.
Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP shows no occupancy over rs73706717.
The C allele does not change enhancer activity or MYC expression in HCT116-derived assays.

chains.title: Null: no TF-mediated effect of rs73706717; signal is linked to rs6983267 or another causal variant
predictions: No allele-specific TF occupancy at rs73706717.
No allele-specific enhancer reporter difference for rs73706717 alone.
No allele-specific MYC expression difference after controlling for rs6983267.
The CRC association tracks rs6983267 or another linked variant rather than rs73706717.
falsified_if: Allele-specific TCF7L2 or other TF occupancy is detected at rs73706717 independent of rs6983267.
A reporter carrying only the rs73706717 T vs C alleles shows a reproducible allelic difference.
Conditioning on rs6983267 leaves an independent rs73706717 effect on MYC or CRC risk.

chains.title: TCF7L2 binds ref T more and represses or fails to activate MYC

links.claim: TCF7L2 binds the ref T allele more strongly than the alt C allele; the T>C change disrupts a TCF/LEF-related site in the 8q24 enhancer. This is the opposite allelic direction from H1 and is kept as a lower-probability competitor because the exact motif orientation and sequence context are not supplied.
The variant sits in the 8q24 enhancer, and the ref T allele preserves higher TCF7L2 occupancy and enhancer output.
TCF7L2 occupancy at the ref T allele modulates MYC; if TCF7L2 is repressive or if the enhancer is already saturated, the net effect on MYC may be lower or unchanged.
HCT116 has active Wnt/TCF7L2 signaling, so allele-specific TCF7L2 occupancy can be tested in this cell type.
The ref T allele is associated with the disease-risk direction through altered TCF7L2 occupancy and MYC regulation; the alt C allele isprotective or less risky in this model.

predictions: Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP shows T > C occupancy at rs73706717.
The T allele changes enhancer reporter activity more than C.
MYC expression tracks the T allele in this model.
The T allele is the risk-associated allele.
falsified_if: Direct binding assays show C > T or equal TCF7L2 binding.
Allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP shows C > T occupancy.
Reporter assays show C, not T, drives higher enhancer activity.

chains.title: MYC/MAX binds alt C more at an E-box in the 8q24 enhancer

links.claim: MYC, acting as a MYC/MAX heterodimer, binds the alt C allele more strongly than ref T at a variant E-box-like site in the 8q24 enhancer. This is a lower-probability alternative because MYC is the locus target and E-box motifs can be altered by T>C, but no occupancy evidence for MYC over this exact base is supplied.
The variant lies in the 8q24 enhancer, and the C allele creates or strengthens a MYC/MAX-bound E-box that modulates enhancer activity.
MYC binding at its own 8q24 enhancer contributes to MYC autoregulation; the C allele increases this feedback and raises MYC expression.
HCT116 colorectal carcinoma cells express MYC and have active 8q24 enhancer chromatin, so MYC occupancy can be tested there.
Higher MYC/MAX occupancy at the C allele increases MYC expression and colorectal cancer risk.

predictions: MYC ChIP shows C > T occupancy at rs73706717.
TCF7L2 ChIP shows no allele bias at this base.
The C allele increases enhancer reporter activity in a MYC-dependent manner.
MYC expression is higher on the C allele.
falsified_if: MYC ChIP shows no occupancy or no allele bias over rs73706717.
TCF7L2, not MYC, shows the allele-specific occupancy.
The C allele does not alter MYC expression or enhancer activity.

next_experiment: Competitive EMSA with recombinant TCF7L2 and T vs C probes (or, if occupancy is required, allele-specific TCF7L2 ChIP-qPCR in a heterozygous CRC line). If the C probe shifts more, H1 is supported; if binding is equal or absent, H0 is favored.
